lyrics:
[Intro: warm electric piano, soft strings, laid-back drums]

[Chorus: female voice, sung, hopeful]
If they gave me the keys to the city
Just for a weekend, just for a day
I'd open every door that they painted shut
And I'd give the keys away

[Verse 1: male rap, smooth and deliberate]
First thing: public pool on Ninth, been dry since ninety-eight
I'd fill it up by noon and prop the gate
Second: every fine that's older than the kid who's paying
Gone. Clean. No more court dates, no more praying
Library stays open till the last one leaves
Bus runs all night for the folks with keys
To other people's offices they mop at three
Free ride home. That one's for my auntie.

[Chorus: female voice, sung, hopeful]
If they gave me the keys to the city
Just for a weekend, just for a day
I'd open every door that they painted shut
And I'd give the keys away

[Verse 2: rap, warmer, horns in]
Streetlight on my mother's block, been out a year
Fixed. And the one by the school. Make it clear.
Grocery with real vegetables in walking range
A bench at every stop. That ain't strange.
No statue, no parade, don't name a thing for me
Put a tree where there's a lot. Let it be.
Sunday night I'd drop the ring back on the desk
With a list for Monday. You can do the rest.

[Bridge: female voice over strings]
It wouldn't take a king
It wouldn't take a crown
Just somebody who's walked it
Walking it around

[Final Chorus: female voice, choir behind]
If they gave me the keys to the city
Just for a weekend, just for a day
I'd open every door that they painted shut
And I'd give the keys away

[Outro: electric piano, kids splashing, a bus pulling up]
